title: MetaUAS: Universal Anomaly Segmentation with One-Prompt Meta-Learning
what_it_is: Anomaly segmentation recast as change segmentation between a query and ONE normal prompt image: frozen EfficientNet-b4, soft feature alignment between query and prompt at 3 deep scales, U-Net decoder back to full resolution; meta-trained only on synthetic change pairs from natural-image datasets (full text read).
why_it_could_help_us: Gives a layout-agnostic 'what differs from this normal cell' map: prompt a clean cell of the same layout (a pool half-cell for half-cut cells) and feed the map as an extra input channel or 6th ensemble member; or meta-train it on EL change pairs made by pasting our labelled cracks/inactive onto clean cells. Its decoder is full-resolution, unlike patch-NN AD. Paper: MVTec pixel AP 59.3 with 1 prompt vs UniAD full-shot 44.7; VisA 42.7 vs 34.3.
cost_to_try: new pipeline (offline prior), then input channel
risk_or_reason_against: Trained on object-level natural-image changes; VisA PRO 60.4 is far below PatchCore 84.6, so thin low-contrast lines are not shown to work; needs a geometrically similar prompt (cell layout varies by source)

title: MuSc-V2: Zero-Shot Multimodal Industrial Anomaly Classification and Segmentation With Mutual Scoring of Unlabeled Samples
what_it_is: Zero-shot AD: every unlabelled test sample scores the patches of every other sample (nearest-patch distance, interval average of the lowest X%); normal patches find many matches, anomalies stay isolated; V2 adds neighbourhood aggregation, 3D fusion, re-scoring (full text, method + results read).
why_it_could_help_us: Matches the unseen-module setting exactly: score all cells of one new module against each other, no labels and no reference set from our pool needed, so the half-cut layout and the module's own contrast are 'normal' by construction. Map = recall prior for the crack/inactive heads on unseen modules. Paper: splitting the data into 2-3 subsets loses at most 1.0-1.2% AP.
risk_or_reason_against: ViT patch scores upsampled from a 37x37-type grid, so 1-2 px cracks become 8-30 px blobs; repeated module-wide defects (e.g. inactive in many cells) are not isolated and get low scores; 2D-only gains of V2 over V1 not isolated in what I read

title: Supervised Anomaly Detection for Complex Industrial Images (SegAD, Valeo VAD)
what_it_is: Per-segment statistics (99.5% quantile, skew, kurtosis, mean) of one or more anomaly maps, plus a supervised classifier score, fed to a boosted random forest for an image-level decision (full text read).
why_it_could_help_us: Only paper found that measures what an AD map adds on top of a supervised model on real defects incl. unseen ones: WRN classifier FPR@95TPR 32.8 -> 16.4 with AD maps + WRN + SegAD; unseen-defect score distribution moves up to that of seen defects. Supports using an AD map per structural segment (busbar zone, cell edge, half-cut gap) as an input to a cell-level 'missed defect' flag.
risk_or_reason_against: Image-level only, no pixel output; gains measured on one product with a static layout; we need pixel masks under relF1@2

title: ISP-AD: a large-scale real-world dataset for advancing industrial anomaly detection with synthetic and real defects
what_it_is: Screen-printing dataset with small, weak-contrast defects on structured patterns; supervised patch classifier trained on a balanced stream of clean + synthetic-defect patches into which real defects are injected with probability p_inj (1/32) (full text read).
why_it_could_help_us: Structured periodic background like cell fingers/busbars. Shows that a synthetic defect stream plus few real defects beats either alone and recovers defect classes the generator cannot make: LSM-1 recall 76.8 -> 95.8 (FN 22 -> 4) with 172 real; ASM MCC 0.70 -> 0.97. Recipe for us: keep 532 real cells, add a model-free synthetic dark-line / dark-region stream on clean pool cells incl. 1,152 half-cells, at a controlled injection rate.
risk_or_reason_against: Image/patch-level classification, not pixel seg; our crack copy-paste and synthetic half-cuts (HC, HC2) already failed, so the gain hinges on the injection control, not on synthesis itself

title: Explicit Boundary Guided Semi-Push-Pull Contrastive Learning for Supervised Anomaly Detection (BGAD)
what_it_is: Normalizing flow on normal features gives an explicit boundary set by the normal distribution only; a semi-push-pull loss pulls normal features inside and pushes the few known anomalies beyond a margin, so known anomalies do not bias the detector (full text read).
why_it_could_help_us: Auxiliary 'defect vs normal' flow head on HRNet features with crack/inactive pixels as known anomalies; the decision boundary depends on normal pixels only, so defects that look unlike training cracks (unseen modules) should still fall outside. Paper Table 4: trained on one anomaly class, pixel AUROC on other classes 0.994 -> 0.995 (carpet), 0.966 -> 0.975 (metal nut), i.e. no loss on unseen classes; MVTec pixel AUROC/PRO 0.992/0.976.
risk_or_reason_against: Gains are in AUROC at 0.97-0.99, not in tolerant F1 on thin lines; flow on 1/4-res features may still be too coarse for 1-2 px cracks; adds a second scoring path to fuse

title: GMMSeg: Gaussian Mixture Based Generative Semantic Segmentation Models
what_it_is: Replaces the softmax classifier with per-class Gaussian mixtures over pixel features (EM-updated) while training the network discriminatively; the same model scores unknown pixels by low likelihood (full text, results read).

Several mixture components per class fit multi-modal classes (a crack looks different in each of 5 sources and on mono vs multi). Likelihood gives an unknown-region map on E1 (scuff, cut edge) with no extra data, to stop false cracks.

Paper: FPR 0.85-17.7 and AuPRC +7 over SOTA on Fishyscapes/SMIYC/RoadAnomaly while inlier seg is frozen.

title: Improving Semantic Segmentation via Efficient Self-Training (CSST)
what_it_is: Offline teacher pseudo-labels large unlabelled sets; centroid sampling crops patches around the centroid of every class region so rare classes appear each epoch; fast crop-size schedule (full text, method + Cityscapes results read).
why_it_could_help_us: Self-training that worked at FULL labels: Cityscapes +1.2 (pseudo-labels 1:1) to +1.9 (7:1) over a 78.1 teacher; students of other architectures +1.7 to +3.9; centroid sampling is worth +1.1 and without it more pseudo-labels hurt (78.9 -> 78.7). Our SSL null used online Mean Teacher without class-centroid crops. Arm: C2 ensemble as teacher on the 11.9k pool incl. 1,152 half-cells, crops centred on pseudo crack/inactive components, 7:1 pseudo:real.
risk_or_reason_against: Teacher errors on half-cut cells are exactly the E1 failure, so pseudo-labels there may be wrong; D29 already lists offline-teacher self-training (Zoph P051, Noisy Student P180); CSST adds the rare-class sampler
